data.title: O-I Glass surges as Citi upgrades to Buy after YTD plunge
data.description:
O-I Glass (OI) up 10.4% in Friday's trading as Citi upgraded the manufacturer of glass containers to Buy from Neutral with a $9 price target, raised from $8, with a 90-day catalyst watch, saying the shares look meaningfully oversold after falling 57% YTD.

O-I Glass (OI) has been hit with higher energy costs from the Middle East conflict, operational issues leading to lower Fit-to-Win cost savings and higher costs, and a weaker European market on both demand and price, and Citi analyst Anthony Pettinari said after a series of negative revisions, he expects estimates have largely bottomed, and the low-end of FY 2026 EBITDA guidance could be reiterated on the Q3 earnings call in late October given conservative assumptions for an H2 volume recovery, stabilizing net pricing in Europe, and resolved operational headwinds.

The company updated FY 2026 EBITDA guidance to reflect operational issues leading to lower Fit-to-Win savings and higher costs, but Pettinari said he does not expect any carryover into H2 2026 or H1 2027, noting O-I (OI) closed three European plants in H1, stressing operating rates at other facilities while costs were rising after the start of the Middle East conflict; further, there was a furnace fire in France and a furnace leak in the U.K., and it was forced to pivot someshipping from rail to truck following unexpected disruption in France.

O-I (OI) said it now expects a $75M-$125M drag on EBITDA from lower net price, greater than the $35M-$100M assumed in April, due to heightened competitive pressure in an oversuppliedEuropean glass market, but the analyst expects performance could improve as the company benefits from a lower cost position and increased focus on high-value customers as Fit-to-Win initiatives accelerate in Europe.

data.title: SpaceX expands access to Grok Bot
data.description:
• SpaceX (SPCX) said on Friday that it is expanding access to its artificial intelligence agent, Grok Bot.
  • Previously only available in beta, Grok Bot is now available in all SuperGrok Plus, Cursor Pro+, and Cursor Teams plans, the Elon Musk-led company said on its website. That brings the AI agent to SuperGrok Plus, SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Pro+, Cursor Ultra, and Cursor Teams Plans (both standard and premium).
  • "Grok Bot is designed for people who want agents to handle anything from a project to an entire function," SpaceX added. "They're digital teammates you can message, run in parallel, and trust to finish work in the tools you already use. Bots work across apps and inboxes, keep going when you step away, and only pull you in for judgment calls."
  • Grok Bot is already capable of handling jobs such as a website builder, office manager, game artist, customer support, and more, SpaceX added.

data.title: Fannie Mae sees senior departures raising concerns over turmoil in firm - report
data.description:
Fannie Mae (FNMA) saw at least 10 senior departures this week, raising concerns over the firm's ability to provide stability to prices and activity, people familiar with the matter told The Wall Street Journal.

Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac (FMCC) buy mortgages in the secondary market, package them as mortgage-backed securities, and sell them to investors. The activity empowers lenders to make more 30-year fixed-rate mortgages.

The departures include many of the company's top leaders, and some weren't by choice. Several officials were told that their positions were eliminated, according to the sources.

The news comes amid an already uncertain outlook for the housing market. 

The U.S. Treasury Department announced it will at least double the maximum size of its liquidity-support buyback operations for longer-dated nominal coupon securities. The move arrived as the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield touched levels not seen since 2007 on fiscal and inflation concerns. Following the announcement, longer-term yields retreated.

data.title: A U.S. government lab wants to know if Chinese LiDAR is a national security risk -- TechCrunch
data.description:
The U.S. government is looking into the risks using Chinese light detection and ranging ((LiDAR)) technology in U.S autonomous vehicles presents to both national security and drivers’ safety, potentially closing a the remaining loophole against using of Chinese technology in domestically manufactured vehicles.

According to TechCrunch, citing sources familiar with the matter, the Idaho National Laboratory, a federally funded research facility owned by the Department of Energy, is reportedly conducting a study on how the technology could transmit sensitive information back to Beijing or even be powered down, disabling vehicles across the country.

The study is reportedly being funded by a company, or group of companies, in the electric and autonomous vehicle industry.

Through the use of pulsed laser light, LiDAR provides a high-resolution picture of a vehicle’s surroundings that can determine the distance between objects and build precise, three-dimensional maps of objects and environments. Although the technology was once prohibitively expensive compared to cameras and radar (used by Tesla), Chinese LiDAR manufacturers like Hesai (HSAI) and RoboSense (RBSTF) have brought the cost down dramatically thanks to lower labor costs and economies of scale in China. Unable to keep up with Chinese competitors, American LiDAR manufacturers have either gone bankrupt, like Luminar, or merged with peers in the industry, such as Ouster (OUST) and Velodyne.

Currently, the Commerce Department bans the use of Chinese-made connectivity hardware in U.S. passenger cars, giving an exception to LiDAR and other autonomous vehicle sensors.

That could change, however, as bipartisan measures from U.S. lawmakers aim to prevent the use of Chinese LiDAR in vehicles on American roads.

“We need to be doing more to protect Americans, and that starts with ensuring taxpayer dollars aren’t being used to purchase technologies that could be used to spy on us,” the Democratic senator from Wisconsin, Tammy Baldwin said, who is introducing the Securing Infrastructure from Adversaries Act with Republican Ted Budd of North Carolina.

data.title: Ray Dalio warns of impending U.S. debt crisis, urges gold, bitcoin hedging
data.description:
Billionaire Ray Dalio warned Friday that a severe U.S. sovereign debt crisis could arrive "in three years, give or take two" without significant structural policy adjustments.

In a LinkedIn post, the Bridgewater Associates founder urged a major portfolio reassessment as the U.S.'s fiscal trajectory worsens. This warning is consistent with the classic debt-cycle model Dalio outlined in his book How Countries Go Broke, where rising interest payments eventually collide with weak investor demand, forcing central banks to print money and devalue fiat currencies.

The fiscal metrics underlying his warning are notable. With the national debt recently topping $40T, Dalio estimates the U.S. government faces a $2T shortfall this year, with $5.5T in revenue against $7.5T in spending. Interest expenses alone will consume $1T this year, while some $10T of short-dated debt must be refinanced. 

Underweighting bonds (TLT) (IEF) (ZROZ) and holding 10% to 15% of a portfolio in gold (GLD) alongside "a bit" of bitcoin (BTC-USD) is the best way to hedge this risk, Dalio advised.

"I expect non-government-produced monies like gold and bitcoin to do relatively well," he wrote, noting that similar fiscal strains are currently confronting the U.K., China and Japan.

Gold (GLD) and bitcoin (IBIT) are already surging this week as a surprise U.S. Treasury intervention under Secretary Scott Bessent to double long-term bond buybacks renewed "debasement trade" chatter. Gold is on track for its best monthly performance since September 1999, while BTC is on pace for its strongest weekly rally in over three years.

data.title: Nevada approves Tesla, Uber, and Waymo for robotaxi rides around Las Vegas
data.description:
Nevada approved permits for Tesla (TSLA), Uber (UBER), and Waymo (WAYMO) to offer paid robotaxi rides in Clark County. Tesla (TSLA) was approved to operate up to 5K robotaxis by the Transportation Authority, while Waymo (WAYMO) can deploy 1K robotaxis and Uber (UBER) another 1K.

Amazon's Zoox (ZOOX) and Hyundai’s Motional already have an autonomous vehicle network permit that allows them to operate robotaxis. Looking ahead, Uber is (UBER) is partnering with both Zoox (ZOOX) and Hyundai's (HYMTF) on autonomous rides. In the early stages of robotaxi deployment on the Las Vegas Strip, the wait times have been longer than those for a taxi or a regular Uber (UBER) ride, although customer satisfaction ratings have been strong in general.

Shares of Tesla (TSLA) were up 5.5% in Friday afternoon trading. Uber (UBER) edged 0.5% higher.

data.title: HHS seeking public input on vaccine recommendation categories
data.description:
• HHS has issued a formal Request for Information that seeks public input on the categories used in federal vaccine recommendations and how shared decision-making between patients and doctors fits into it.
  • Three categories are currently used: routine (universal), risk-based, and shared clinical decision-making.
  • The agency wants to know if those categories "are adequate, clear, and well understood" and "whether it should adopt additional or different categories."
  • HHS wants the public to weigh in on considerations that could influence recommendations and categories, such as the quality and strength of evidence; informed consent and religious freedom; and how shared clinical decision-making is applied in practice.
  • Vaccine recommendations are made by CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices. However, in May, HHS rescinded ACIP's charter, citing an administrative error. 
  • In March, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was rebuffed by a federal judge who stayed the appointment of 13 new ACIP members as well as changes to the childhood vaccination schedule he wanted.

data.title: SA Asks: Which software companies could be takeover targets?
data.description:
Last week, shares of Workday (WDAY) rallied on reports that the software company might be acquired by private equity firm Silver Lake.

We asked Seeking Alpha analysts Chris DeMuth Jr., The Value Investor, and Kevin Anthony D. Arroyo which software companies they thought could also be potential takeover targets.

Chris DeMuth Jr.: Activists are on a good run pressing managements to run reviews. It looks like Elliott will succeed with their Workday (WDAY) investment if it gets sold to Silver Lake. Next after that? Maybe Jana will get Alkami Technology (ALKT) sold. That process looks promising. 

(Chris DeMuth Jr. leads the SA investing group Sifting the World.) 

The Value Investor: In my view, businesses that are not too large, not too leveraged, and have real potential to use AI to their benefit are prime candidates. These include names like Atlassian (TEAM), Intuit (INTU), Paychex (PAYX), SS&C Technologies (SSNC), and Docusign (DOCU), but with the comment that many of these stocks have rebounded recently, thereby reducing the chance of M&A action.

(The Value Investor leads the SA investing group Value in Corporate Events.)

Kevin Anthony D. Arroyo: The debilitating effect of AI in the software industry, reflected in their valuations, could open the floodgates for incumbent companies to further consolidate their industry. Which is something that they have failed to do in the past due to antitrust concerns and private equity looking for cheap target companies with healthier balance sheets and solid franchises that could be levered up to generate attractive returns. 

The software companies that I find most susceptible to a takeover are the smaller ones that compete in specialized segments or verticals. Names include Monday.com (MNDY) in business management, Appian (APPN) in enterprise process automation, PTC (PTC) in product lifecycle management, Freshworks (FRSH) in ticketing and service management, and DocuSign (DOCU) in document and agreement management.

The bolt-on acquisition characteristics of some of these small companies are a perfect match with the more portfolio-driven business models of some of the big traditional software companies such as Adobe (ADBE), Autodesk (ADSK), and Salesforce (CRM). 

I see private equity going for bigger software companies with healthy balance sheets, established customer and distribution relationships, and a solid churn rate, as they would likely provide stable and resilient cash flows despite the potential disruption from AI.

data.title: SA analyst upgrades/downgrades: AAPL, AAP, AMD, LOW
data.description:
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) earned an upgrade to Buy from Future Stack Investment, fueled by explosive data center revenue growth tied to the AI infrastructure boom. Advance Auto Parts (AAP) also received a Buy upgrade from Seeking Profits following a sharp share price decline, with margin recovery viewed as underappreciated by the market.

On the downgrade front, Apple (AAPL) was cut to Sell by Bay Area Ideas amid valuation concerns and mounting margin pressures, while Lowe's (LOW) was downgraded to Hold by Albert Anthony despite delivering consecutive earnings beats, as housing market headwinds cloud the near-term outlook.

Upgrades

  • Advanced Micro Devices (AMD): Upgrade Hold to Buy by Future Stack Investment. The analyst highlights AMD's dramatic transformation in its data center business, with AI-related products now driving the majority of revenue and creating a powerful, self-reinforcing growth cycle.

"The valuation remains demanding, and it's not a low-risk Buy. Overall, I think the basic picture has strengthened substantially to the point where I'm convinced that the expected upside outweighs the valuation risk."

  • Advance Auto Parts (AAP): Upgrade to Buy by Seeking Profits. Following a 25% share price decline, the analyst sees significant opportunity in the company's underappreciated margin recovery and turnaround progress under new management.

"The auto parts retailer has undergone a meaningful transformation under new management, closing unprofitable stores, shedding noncore businesses, and improving the health of its balance sheet...With updated financials, now is a good time to see if the recovery thesis is broken or if the dramatic move has created an opportunity."

Downgrades

  • Apple (AAPL): Downgrade Hold to Sell by Bay Area Ideas. The analyst argues that Apple's valuation premium is no longer justified given decelerating growth, component cost pressures, and expected gross margin contraction in the coming quarter.

"Despite receding from the recent peak, Apple's forward P/E ratio is at a reading of 35.93. That represents a bit of expansion from the 34.10 reading that's found in my previous update. With the valuation having gotten more expensive but the outlook deteriorating for the company, I believe that the risk/reward setup has now become bearish."

  • Lowe's Companies (LOW): Downgrade Buy to Hold by Albert Anthony. Despite another earnings beat and strong online sales growth, the analyst cites challenging margin trends and sector headwinds from a sluggish housing market as reasons for a more cautious stance.

"Market momentum has not been too confident on this stock since around springtime, and it continues to severely underperform a major benchmark like the S&P 500, without a sign of a recovery emerging. So, I don't expect it to achieve alpha anytime soon, and this hurts any confidence in a bull case."
